round: A (zero-velocity) + B (cross-window velocity state) + C (heteroscedastic uncertainty), 2026-09-25

code.tools/train_physnet.py: stillness head (--still-weight), structural ZUPT gate (--gate), two-pass ZUPT re-anchoring (--zupt), heteroscedastic log-variance head (--nll-weight), predict_streams
code.tools/fuse_trajectory.py: session-level least squares over node positions with displacement, velocity and zero-velocity edges; reference or gyroscope attitude; re-reads the 3-s displacements from the fused trajectory
code.tools/zupt_bound.py: physical accuracy of zero-velocity-aided strapdown integration between detected still phases
code.tools/eval_uncertainty.py: coverage, sharpness, discrimination and recalibration of the predicted uncertainty
code.tools/eval_session_cv.py: --baseline-tag so a new PhysNet fold set can be compared against existing baseline folds

A_zero_velocity.stillness_labels: still < 3 mm/s, moving > 8 mm/s, the band between is not supervised; 27 % of supervised training frames are still, 61 % of training windows and 16.5 % of validation windows contain at least one still frame
A_zero_velocity.verdict: the gate improves the mean by 0.26 mm (within the 1.6 mm seed spread of the reference) but halves that spread and clearly improves the sealed-test metrics; the two-pass re-anchoring is not adopted because it does not combine with the gate

data_hygiene.note: excluding the two rigidity recordings that fail the mount test (done by tools/prepare_trajectory_data.py) is worth more than any architecture change in this round

pose_graph_with_velocity_and_zupt_edges.result: no effect: re-read validation error 29.67 -> 29.7-29.9 mm and ATE 78-80 mm for every weight combination
pose_graph_with_velocity_and_zupt_edges.reason: tens of thousands of displacement edges dominate a few hundred neighbour edges, and the velocity stream is not identified in absolute terms unless it is supervised

zupt_aided_strapdown_bound.verdict: zero-velocity-aided integration is accurate only below about 2 s (about 1 mm) and diverges beyond 4 s because attitude error leaks gravity (1 deg gives 0.17 m/s2, i.e. 0.77 m over 3 s); the 3-s protocol cannot be rescued this way, and the present recordings contain too few pauses (the sealed test session has one still segment)

C_uncertainty.accuracy_cost: none: gate+NLL 30.09 mm versus gate 30.42 mm on validation
C_uncertainty.variance_weighted_fusion: no effect on ATE (68.0 -> 68.2 and 86.7 -> 85.6 mm)

final_protocol_cvg.config: PhysNet, weight decay 0.1, dense supervision, still-weight 1, structural gate, extra_train = 4 verified rigid sessions, 8 folds x 2 seeds
final_protocol_cvg.trade_off: the gate improves every local metric (test 44.39 -> 43.55 mm, fast third 75.15 -> 72.67 mm, R2 0.215 -> 0.252, blend 42.60 -> 42.21 mm and R2 0.256 -> 0.276) but degrades trajectory ATE (87.8 -> 109.8 mm, blend 81.1 -> 90.8 mm) because suppressing motion increases shrinkage, which the mean local error rewards and the accumulated error penalizes; the non-gated fold ensemble remains the best trajectory estimator (80.7 mm)

best_sealed_test_local_err_mm.method: PhysNet(gate)+IMUNet equal blend, CV fold ensembles

conclusions: Zero-velocity information is the only mechanism found so far that moves the sealed-test metrics beyond seed noise, and the detector itself is reliable (recall 0.94-1.0, false alarm 0-0.02).

Its benefit is bounded by how often the camera actually stops: the present recordings contain 0.5-2.3 still segments per minute, which is why the gain is 1 mm rather than the 15 mm the physics allows.

Classical ZUPT-aided integration is accurate to about 1 mm below 2 s but diverges beyond 4 s from gravity leakage, so it cannot replace the learned estimator at the 3-s horizon; this quantifies the boundary between the model-based and learned regimes.
Heteroscedastic uncertainty is free in accuracy, needs one scale factor, and then provides usable per-prediction intervals with a 4.3x error separation between the most and least confident deciles.
Mean local error and accumulated trajectory error select different operating points; both must be reported.
